steps.u: Move the users table from MySQL to Postgres. About 12 million rows. Minimal downtime please.

steps.r: CREATE TABLE users (id INT AUTO_INCREMENT, email VARCHAR(255), created DATETIME, flags TINYINT(1) ...)

steps.a: Type differences to handle: AUTO_INCREMENT becomes an identity column, DATETIME has no time zone so it must be interpreted as UTC explicitly, and TINYINT(1) flags become booleans. For minimal downtime I will bulk load a snapshot, then replay changes from the binlog until cutover.

i.content: CREATE TABLE users (id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, email text, created timestamptz, is_active boolean);
1. Pause writes 2. Replay final binlog 3. Verify counts 4. Switch connection string 5. Keep MySQL read-only for a week

reference.summary: Prepared a MySQL to Postgres migration of a 12 million row users table: mapped types, bulk loaded with pgloader with matching counts and a checksum sample, and wrote a cutover plan with change replay and a week of read-only fallback.
facts: MySQL to Postgres for the users table
12 million rows copied with no errors
type mapping for identity, time zone and booleans

decisions.choice: bulk load a snapshot then replay changes before cutover
decisions.reason: it keeps the downtime window short
